Work with packs.

## Commands

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`cuilo pack list`](#cuilo-pack-list) | List the packs and their pieces. |
| [`cuilo pack show`](#cuilo-pack-show) | Show a pack's pieces and their inputs. |
| [`cuilo pack add`](#cuilo-pack-add) | Load and verify a pack from a source, e.g. `gh:acme/packs@v1.2.0`, `./packs/mine` or `registry:https://…/card.json`. |
| [`cuilo pack capture`](#cuilo-pack-capture) | Turn project files into a new piece of a local pack. |

## cuilo pack list

List the packs and their pieces.

### Usage

```sh
cuilo pack list [OPTIONS]
```

## cuilo pack show

Show a pack's pieces and their inputs.

### Usage

```sh
cuilo pack show [OPTIONS] <PACK>
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<PACK>` | Pack name. |

## cuilo pack add

Load and verify a pack from a source, e.g. `gh:acme/packs@v1.2.0`, `./packs/mine` or `registry:https://…/card.json`.

### Usage

```sh
cuilo pack add [OPTIONS] <SOURCE>
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<SOURCE>` | The source. |

## cuilo pack capture

Turn project files into a new piece of a local pack.

### Usage

```sh
cuilo pack capture [OPTIONS] --piece <PIECE> <FILES>...
```

### Arguments

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<FILES>` | Project files to capture. Repeatable. |

### Options

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--piece <PIECE>` | Name of the new piece. |
| `--name <SPELLING>` | How the name is spelled in the files, e.g. `UserCard`; it becomes the `name` input. |
| `--pack-dir <PACK_DIR>` | Folder of the pack to write into. Default: `packs/local`. |
| `--pack <PACK>` | Pack name when that folder has no pack yet. Default: `local`. |
| `--dry-run` | Only show the plan. |
| `-y, --yes` | Apply without asking; with --verify, also run the checks without asking. |
| `--review` | Choose hunk by hunk what to keep, like `git add -p`. |
| `--diff` | Show diffs of changed files. |
| `--force` | Replace existing files that differ. |
| `--verify` | Before applying, run the project's checks on a throwaway copy with the plan applied; apply only when none fails because of the plan. Code from the pack can run there, so the checks start only after you see the plan and agree, or with --yes. |
| `--install` | After applying, add the packages the plan lists with the project's package manager. |
| `--no-install` | Never offer to add the packages the plan lists. |

## Global options

`--root`, `--json` and `--no-input` work here too; see [global options](/reference/cli/#global-options).
